artworks.title: Cadmus Killing the Dragon
artworks.description: Zuccarelli's Arcadian kill: Cadmus spears Ares' serpent at the spring — Ovid's bloody prelude to the sowing that will found Thebes.

artworks.title: Cadmus Sowing the Dragon's Teeth
artworks.artist: Workshop of Peter Paul Rubens (after Jacob Jordaens)
artworks.description: Rijksmuseum panel: Cadmus, guided by Minerva, watches the Spartoi rise from the furrows and turn on one another — the prodigy that seeds Thebes.

artworks.title: Two Followers of Cadmus Devoured by a Dragon
artworks.description: Haarlem Mannerist canvas: the Ismenian dragon tears Cadmus' companions while the founder fights on — the price paid before the teeth are sown.

artworks.title: Cadmus and Harmonia
artworks.description: De Morgan's Pre-Raphaelite close: Cadmus and Harmonia become entwined serpents — the Theban founder ending as the dragon he once slew.

popCulture.title: Cadmus
popCulture.description: The Phoenician who sows the dragon's teeth — Cadmus remains the founder-name of Thebes and its doomed house.

popCulture.title: Theban Cycle
popCulture.description: The epic cycle that begins with Cadmus' city and ends in Oedipus' line — Thebes as tragedy's second Troy.
